basis: Source-audited payload and conservative peak bounds; no full-stack allocator measurement
assumptions: 32x32 BFP8/BFP4 tiles occupy 1088/576 bytes including exponent storage; each is already 64-byte aligned.
All 30 layers and 262144 absolute paged tokens retained; no sliding cache truncation. B1 maximum context does not imply 32 simultaneous maximum contexts.

8 MiB per layer covers retained norms, replicated router, two position tables and small metadata tensors. Expert BF16 originals and packed BF16 setup copies are released after each constructor returns; source proof is in memory_audit.md.
Embedding/LM-head allowance is one shared tied BF16 tensor replicated per device, not two separate copies.
RoPE allowance assumes prefill and decode tables shared across layers of each attention kind: two kinds times two layouts times cos/sin. Per-layer copies would exceed capacity.
Long prefill adds input, retained chunk outputs and final concatenated BF16 output: 3*262144*2816*2 = 4429185024 bytes, in addition to the independent 2 GiB reserve.
2 GiB reserve remains for trace regions, chunk-local workspaces, allocator padding, semaphores and unmodelled runtime overhead; no measured allocator peak is claimed.
Normal full-stack scheduling releases previous-layer full outputs and setup containers. Retaining diagnostic outputs or caller weight copies changes the bound.
Conservative peak fits decimal 32 GB and 32 GiB arithmetically; actual usable DRAM, allocator fragmentation, CCL/trace allocations and full-context execution still require validation.

setup_transients_per_device.lifetime: One layer constructor; PackedExperts and active OptimizedExperts retain no original source weight container. Other small setup/allocator overhead remains in the separate reserve.

hypothetical_dual_expert_layout.description: Keep TP4 decode experts and separate EP4 prefill experts, with shared attention, router, norms and shared MLP.
